claims.claim: Original Ambro Brother embroidery Sewing machine.

Photo 0 shows the machine looks generally intact, but durability/strength cannot be verified from a single image.

risks.risk: Whether it actually works (motor, timing, feed, needle/presser operation) and sews cleanly.
risks.proof: A short video of the machine running with the foot pedal (or power on), plus a close-up of stitching on fabric.
risks.if_unproven: Price as not guaranteed to work / needs servicing.

risks.risk: Whether it is truly an embroidery-capable setup (attachments/hoop system) vs a regular sewing machine.
risks.proof: Photos of the embroidery-specific parts (hoop/holder, embroidery foot/guide) and a stitching demo showing embroidery pattern output.
risks.if_unproven: Price as a basic sewing machine (not embroidery-capable).

risks.risk: Exact model and compatibility of parts (needle type, bobbin type, accessories).
risks.proof: Clear photo of the model/serial plate and a photo of the bobbin case/needle plate markings.
risks.if_unproven: Price at the lowest comparable for unknown model/parts availability.

risks.risk: Condition issues not visible in the photo (worn feed dogs, bent needle bar, missing accessories, electrical faults).
risks.proof: Close-ups of needle area, feed mechanism, and any included accessories list; plus a test run.
risks.if_unproven: Price assuming possible missing accessories and/or minor faults.

proof_requests: Send a video of the machine sewing (start to finish) showing neat stitches on fabric.
Send clear photos of the model/serial plate (or any label) and the bobbin/needle plate area.
Show any embroidery attachments/hoop system included (if it’s truly embroidery-capable).
Confirm what accessories are included (needles, bobbins, foot pedal, power cable, presser feet).
response.reason: From photo 0 I can identify the machine brand text (“AIG BROTHER”), but I cannot verify that it is embroidery-capable or that it works and sews neatly; those are the key factors that determine the correct price.
